prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map separates the camera wearer’s forearms and hands at roughly 0.25–0.6 m from the green work surface/bin at about 0.5–1.0 m, with the standing person across it roughly 1–2 m away; the two people are therefore separated by approximately 1–2 m. The wearer’s arms remain low and central, while the other person is mainly ahead and toward the upper-right or upper-left as the camera turns; heads are outside the frame, so facing and gaze cannot be determined. Across the five frames, the wearer’s hands move together toward the cloth and rise slightly, while lateral shifts of the work surface and background indicate turning more clearly than approach or retreat. Compared with RGB, brightness makes near/far layering and arm’s-reach regions easier to see, but the smooth, inconsistent depths around hands, cloth, body boundaries, and the dark background make metre estimates and occlusion ordering unreliable.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map separates several people from the central work surface and small items, supporting left/right and overlap relationships even where RGB colors are similar: the camera wearer occupies much of the lower foreground, another person is across the surface, and partial people or limbs enter near the upper and side edges. The wearer’s hands, cloth, and nearest surface are within roughly 0.3–1.0 m, while the person across is approximately 1–2 m away; heads are cropped, so gaze and precise facing remain unavailable, although torso placement indicates that person is generally across from the wearer. Over time, the large foreground person mask shifts from left/center toward the right, the surface remains between the people, and edge fragments appear or disappear as the camera turns and bodies occlude one another. The masks expose object boundaries and partial occlusions more clearly than RGB, but many labels are plainly unreliable—the work surface/bin is called “suitcase,” and small regions are labelled “scissors” or “pizza”—while several bodies and objects are merged, fragmented, or omitted.
descriptions.pose: The pose map isolates the camera wearer’s hands against black, placing them in the near foreground at roughly 0.25–0.6 m and showing that they move from separated left/right positions toward a closer, more central two-handed configuration before shifting toward the upper-right in the fifth frame. These hand skeletons clarify finger orientation, overlap, and which visible hand parts are within the wearer’s arm’s reach more clearly than RGB; no other person’s reliable hand or body skeleton is consistently shown. Because body keypoints are absent and heads are out of view, the map cannot establish people’s full posture, facing direction, gaze, separation, or whether objects are within another person’s reach. Several fingers are fused, displaced, or missing where the cloth and hands occlude each other, and the lack of a skeleton in the first frame and of yellow body poses across the strip makes temporal tracking incomplete.
